name: a-flash-digicam-birthday
prompt: A candid snapshot taken around 2003 on a cheap pocket digital camera with a tiny sensor, held at arm's length by an uncle at a child's birthday party after dark in a small, overcrowded front room. Close and off-centre to the left, the frame tipped about ten degrees: a seven-year-old with a missing front tooth and a lopsided gold paper crown leans over a homemade chocolate cake, cheeks puffed, mid-blow, the candle flames bending away. Squashed in behind are cousins and a grandmother with hands raised mid-clap and mouths open in a cheer, one boy pulling a face, one auntie's pupils glowing red from the flash. The little built-in flash fires straight on, bleaching the nearest faces and the white tablecloth almost to blank, flattening noses, throwing short hard shadows on the wall behind heads, and falling off fast so the far half of the room sinks into a muddy amber gloom lit only by a fringed lamp. Clutter everywhere: half-deflated foil and latex balloons on the ceiling, a bowl of crisps, plastic beakers of orange squash, torn wrapping paper on a busy swirly brown-and-mustard carpet. Colours are loud and oversaturated with a faint green tint in the shadows, highlights clipped, fine grainy sensor noise and soft blocky compression in the dark areas, slight softness from a cheap lens. Messy, noisy, completely happy. No text, no date stamp, no lettering, no logos anywhere in the image. Thanks.
